svg.metadata: {"concept_id": "edu.eight-phase-lunar-sequence", "source_master_path": "tactile/masters/education/astronomy/moon-and-eclipses/eight-phase-lunar-sequence.svg", "source_master_sha256": "74d29d8fdd760980432c0a135ca1ce4013868515a55bd66e2dd3601a8a4eb7ec", "page_fit_revision": {"status": "regenerated", "method": "Explicit mathematical construction in millimetres; original physical strokes retained and Index dots freshly placed. No export scaling.", "simplification": "Meaning-specific reconstruction with original 1.4 mm strokes and freshly sampled 1.2 mm Index dots. All eight phases keep the clockwise order from the top: new, waxing crescent, first quarter, waxing gibbous, full, waning gibbous, third quarter, waning crescent. One 13 mm vertical stroke now marks the illuminated part, replacing two horizontal hatches; new has none. Crescent and gibbous terminators are deliberately widened toward the middle so the stroke and gaps fit. This teaches phase categories and illumination side, not exact illuminated fractions or 45-degree phase samples. Terminators still stop before the outer limb. Waxing is illuminated on the right and waning on the left in the retained northern upright convention. The sequence repeats one Moon; phases are not caused by Earth shadow.", "canvas_mm": [170, 180]}, "teaching": "All eight phases keep the clockwise order from the top: new, waxing crescent, first quarter, waxing gibbous, full, waning gibbous, third quarter, waning crescent. One 13 mm vertical stroke now marks the illuminated part, replacing two horizontal hatches; new has none. Crescent and gibbous terminators are deliberately widened toward the middle so the stroke and gaps fit. This teaches phase categories and illumination side, not exact illuminated fractions or 45-degree phase samples. Terminators still stop before the outer limb. Waxing is illuminated on the right and waning on the left in the retained northern upright convention. The sequence repeats one Moon; phases are not caused by Earth shadow.
